summary: Asia and Europe opened the week after Friday's AI-led sell-off with mixed results: Taiwan's MediaTek rose 10.0% and ASM International 8.3% in a partial chip rebound, while Samsung Electronics fell 3.1% and SK Hynix 2.5% in Seoul; Tokyo was closed for a holiday. Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, according to its SEC filing, and the COP31 climate summit in Antalya ended without a deal on a fossil-fuel roadmap. The ECB's Monday fixings put the Brazilian real near 6.00 per dollar (+4.9% in a week) and the yen at 159.07, with the Korean won weaker at 1,348.85. US stocks, commodities and rates are unchanged from Friday's close (20 Nov) because US trading was still open when this edition ran; US futures could not be confirmed.
